conference.route: Code du travail D5221-2-1 exemption (3 months or less)
conference.detail: Paid work of 3 months or less needs no work authorisation if it is: a cultural, artistic or scientific event; a colloquium, seminar or trade fair (linked to the event or accredited by the organiser); performing or crew work on a production; or occasional teaching as an invited professor. The Code du travail applies in the overseas departments, but local application and visa rules for the territory should still be confirmed.
conference.next: Keep the organiser's accreditation or invitation; check the visa for this territory.

paid-speaking.route: French work authorisation where French law requires one; the visa exemption doesn't cover it
paid-speaking.detail: The French arrêté on entry to this territory exempts Australians from a visa except for paid activity needing a French work authorisation (autorisation de travail) that the traveller can't show at the border. A paid talk may fall in that category.
paid-speaking.next: Ask the host to check with the territory's DEETS/DREETS (labour authority) whether the paid appearance needs an autorisation de travail, and get the answer in writing.
